title: What MongoDB is
idea: MongoDB is a database that stores each record as a document: a JSON-like object that can hold nested objects and arrays.
points: Documents live in collections, which play the role of SQL tables.
By default, documents in one collection need not share the same fields.
Rules are optional. Mongoose, covered soon, adds a schema in your app.
MongoDB stores documents as BSON, a binary form of JSON with extra types.

head: SQL

What changes
rows: Documents in one collection can differ in shape.
A document can nest objects and arrays.
Fields are not declared up front.
Related data often sits inside the document.
A collection appears on the first insert.
hero.caption: Most SQL ideas have a MongoDB twin. The third column is where the two models differ.

code.title: Three shapes, one collection
code.caption: The official `mongodb` driver. No table is declared first; three differently shaped documents go in, and each gets an `_id`.

pitfalls: Optional schemas still need design: agree on field names and types early.
Field names are case-sensitive: `year` and `Year` are two different fields.
Do not embed lists that grow without limit; a document has a size limit.

quiz.q: You insert `{ title: 'Emma' }` into a `books` collection whose other documents have a `year`. What happens?
options: It is stored as it is
quiz.why: A collection has no fixed fields unless you add validation rules. A missing field is simply absent, not null.

takeaway: A collection holds documents; each document carries its own fields.
